A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching title, authors, methods, and principal experiments. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, classification, contrastive-training, dimension-attribution, and LLM truncation experiments, with outcomes in Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a T5 training-seed robustness experiment in Appendix A.1 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: Random and last-K truncation, single-dimension attribution, contrastive training, and LLM hidden-state/unembedding truncation remain unchanged. The added training replications and procedural clarifications introduce no new method component.

E1.justification: The retrieval and classification datasets, training and analysis corpora, and six LLM evaluation tasks are retained. The new seed experiment reuses NanoBEIR without adding a task, domain, or input scenario; Table 6 is unchanged.

E2.justification: The PCA comparison in Table 2, full-size and truncation controls, and preliminary standard-versus-MRL MPNet comparison are retained. The concurrent work newly discussed in Section 5 is not added as an experimentally evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.1 evaluates the contrastively fine-tuned T5 replicas across truncation sizes, extending beyond Figure 3's controlled comparison of full and half-sized embeddings across training checkpoints. Existing protocols remain; the newly stated convergence stopping rule and last-K choice clarify previously undocumented settings.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 and Figure 7 add a focused robustness analysis asking whether truncation behavior depends on randomness during T5 contrastive training. Existing geometric, outlier, dimension-removal, shared-dimension, and ranking analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports T5 training replications with seeds 42, 727, and 1122 and plots their curves separately. The existing ten-random-removal repetitions and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; this is not a reported increase in repetitions of those earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–4 and the existing plots are retained. New Figure 7 shows nearly overlapping T5 truncation-response curves across three training seeds. The Limitations section also adds that the existing MRL pilot showed relative-performance changes across truncation levels comparable to non-MRL encoders.

T1.justification: Definitions and criteria for anisotropy, dimensional collapse, outlier dimensions, and degrading dimensions are retained. No mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about truncation robustness, degrading dimensions, and task-dependent LLM behavior. The new seed evidence supports these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges that single-dimension attribution does not examine interactions among dimensions and explains the computational barrier. Section 4 also qualifies effective-space-use interpretations as dependent on the tested concepts and phrases the proposed E5-Mistral explanation more cautiously.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project/code-access URL to the abstract's existing code statement. Section 3.1 newly specifies stopping at validation-loss convergence and using last-K truncation, also clarified in Section 3.2. These are additional disclosures rather than evidence that retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Tsukagoshi and Sasano (2025) and a substantive comparison with their prompt-based embedding study. It positions the present work through broader model coverage, controlled training trajectories, and dimension attribution, while retaining the previous related-work discussion.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and acronym corrections, clarifies experimental prose, expands related work and limitations, and inserts Appendix A.1. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the seed-comparison plot as Figure 7. V1 Figures 7–12 are retained as Figures 8–13, with the ranking figure moving to a separate appendix page. Added text and the new figure cause limited layout reflow without redesigning existing figures or tables.

improvement.justification: The three-seed T5 check adds limited support for robustness to training randomness, while procedural disclosures and the code-access pointer improve reproducibility information. Acknowledging untested dimension interactions and discussing concurrent work improve interpretation and positioning. These are useful but bounded gains: the principal evidence and claims remain unchanged, and the underlying cause of degrading dimensions remains unresolved.
